stages.name: Fiscal policy and the budget
stages.title: Fiscal policy and the budget
stages.sub: How the government raises money through tax, how that differs from monetary policy, and what a budget deficit or surplus means.

steps.q: The government wants to slow down spending in the economy. Instead of changing interest rates, it takes a bigger slice of people's wages and firms' profits. What tool is it using?
steps.right: Raising the amount it collects from incomes and profits
steps.wrong: Raising the cost of borrowing money
steps.hint: Interest rates belong to a different policy. What is the government collecting here?

steps.q: One government body sets interest rates to influence borrowing and spending. A different government body sets tax rates and decides how much to spend on schools and hospitals. Are these the same policy or two separate policies?
steps.right: Two separate policies, run by different tools
steps.wrong: The same policy, just described differently
steps.hint: Interest rates and tax/spending are controlled through different instruments, by different bodies.

steps.q: Some taxes are taken straight from a worker's wages or a firm's profits, before the money is even spent. Other taxes are only paid when someone actually buys something in a shop. What decides which of these two groups a tax falls into?
steps.right: Whether it is charged on earning money or on spending it
steps.wrong: Whether the government or a shop collects the cash
steps.hint: Think about the moment the tax is taken: when money is earned, or when it is spent.

steps.q: A worker's pay slip shows money taken straight from their wages, based on their income, before they receive it. Which of the two groups does this belong to?
steps.right: The tax charged on earning income or profit
steps.wrong: The tax charged on spending in shops
steps.hint: Is this taken when the money is earned, or when it is spent?

steps.right: The tax charged on spending in shops
steps.wrong: The tax charged on earning income or profit

steps.q: This year the government spends £700bn but only collects £650bn in tax. Has it taken in more than it spent, or less?
steps.hint: Compare the £650bn collected with the £700bn spent.
steps.pre: Spending more than is collected in tax is a government budget
